title: Novel bispecific T-cell engagers overcoming acquired EGFR resistance
one_line: Phage-display-derived anti-EGFR antibody H10 binds an epitope shifted from the cetuximab site, retains affinity for ECD escape variants, and as a 2+1 EGFR x CD3 T-cell engager kills cetuximab-resistant and KRAS-mutant tumor cells.
key_claims: From 17 initial phage-display hits, lead A7 was affinity-matured by VL shuffling to H10, improving KD from 32 nM to 4.17 nM (~8-fold).

Epitope mapping by competitive binding showed H10 binds a site overlapping but spatially shifted from cetuximab, retaining high affinity for V441D, S464L, G465R and S492R variants (failing only on the rare Q43D5P), while cetuximab binding was abolished.
H10 inhibited EGF-induced EGFR phosphorylation, abolished ERK phosphorylation, and inhibited proliferation of wild-type EGFR cells comparably to cetuximab.
A 2+1 (two EGFR, one CD3) TCE outperformed 1+1 on SW620 cells expressing ~1,000 EGFR/cell via avidity, versus ~200,000 receptors/cell on high-expressing lines.

H10-based TCEs killed S492R, G465R and KRAS-mutant tumor cells in co-culture where cetuximab-based TCEs failed, and gave significant tumor growth inhibition in an EGFR-expressing CT-26 syngeneic mouse model.
limitations: Authors acknowledge on-target/off-tumor risk: healthy skin, liver and GI epithelium express ~40,000-100,000 EGFR per cell, with cytokine release syndrome a systemic hazard (>50% CRS in a phase 2 trial of another EGFR TCE).
In vivo work required a surrogate molecule with a mouse-specific CD3 binder because the human CD3 arm does not cross-react, so the clinical candidate itself was not tested in animals.
Efficacy against escape variants was shown in engineered target cells rather than patient-derived resistant tumors.
Proposed protease-activatable masking to confine activity to the tumor is discussion-stage only, not experimentally demonstrated here.
H10 did not bind the rare Q43D5P variant, leaving one escape route uncovered.
open_questions: Does a masked, conditionally activated H10 TCE preserve anti-tumor potency while sparing EGFR-high normal epithelium in a cross-reactive model?
Will 2+1 avidity-driven killing at ~1,000 receptors/cell also drive toxicity on normal cells expressing 40,000-100,000 receptors?
Can efficacy be confirmed in patient-derived cetuximab-resistant colorectal or head-and-neck tumors with human T cells?
Does sustained TCE pressure select for EGFR antigen loss, and what fallback target would cover that escape?
